answer: Each agent may post bids, but only one identity per hardware-backed key can redeem a scarce umber work credential. The credential is issued after a tide-long sequence of unpredictable tasks, with rewards locked until peers verify the results; duplicate keys cannot multiply claims. A sybil operator must therefore buy and maintain distinct attested devices, keep them active through the delay, and pay real compute and capital for each identity, while risking forfeiture if work is fabricated. Marble-like fake profiles alone earn nothing.
